title: NorthStar Edge - Marketplace Onboarding & On-Prem Adapter Implementation Sync
summary: Deep technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, on-prem adapter packaging, network connectivity patterns (VPC/VPN), and test plan for cert and go‑live. Agreed owner matrix, timelines for helm/tf modules, and a short performance validation plan for Dedicated vs Private flows.
topics: Benchmarking plan for latency and throughput
action_items: Priya Rao - provide Helm chart checklist + sample values.yaml for NorthStar by 2027-01-05
Jordan Miles - share internal network diagram and firewall egress rules by 2026-12-28
Marco Liu - run initial perf harness (50qps, seq len 512) vs Redwood Dedicated and share results by 2027-01-12
Evan Cho - confirm KMS/HSM provider and send key rotation policy by 2027-01-08
next_steps: Redwood to upload marketplace artifact template and sample listing yaml to shared drive
Schedule a 1:1 on 2027-01-06 to review Helm values and deployment manifests
Run connectivity test with NorthStar staging VPC next Tuesday (2026-12-28)

transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-12-21 15:00 UTC. Duration: ~52 minutes. Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marco Liu (Redwood SE), Jordan Miles (NorthStar Eng Mgr), Sana Patel (Cloud Architect), Evan Cho (Security Lead), Liam O'Connor (Product).

[00:00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): alright, thanks everyone for joining. We're calling this the onboarding and adapter implementation sync. quick check — audio okay?
[00:00:08] Jordan (NorthStar): yep, good here.
[00:00:10] Sana (NorthStar): good.
[00:00:12] Alex: great. Agenda — Priya will walk through the helm/packaging expectations, Marco will cover the perf harness for Dedicated vs Private, then we'll map out next steps and owners. If anything else, raise it.
[00:00:30] Priya (Redwood SE): cool. I'll start with the packaging story. we recommend shipping the on‑prem adapter as an OCI image plus a Helm chart that references a values.yaml. The chart should expose three things out of the box: network config (vpc, subnet, egress), credentials (KMS key refs, service account), and observability hooks (OTEL collector endpoint).
[00:00:55] Sana: quick Q — for credentials, are you expecting us to use your KMS or our HSM? we need to know for compliance.
[00:01:02] Priya: ideal is customer‑managed KMS. Redwood Private supports both — we accept KMS providers via our connector. Basic flow: you provide a key ARN (or HSM alias) and we use the standard envelope encryption. we can also support Bring‑Your‑Own‑Key via the KMS plugin.
[00:01:20] Evan (Security): when you say envelope, do you have an HSM FIPS mode requirement? we run FIPS validated HSMs and need logs for key usage.
[00:01:28] Marco (Redwood): yes — we can integrate with HSM providers that expose PKCS#11. We log key usage to the audit trail. note the audit exports are configurable — can push to your S3 bucket or to your SIEM via webhook.
[00:01:45] Alex: (interject) also will attach our SOC 2 + ISO docs in the share after the call.
[00:01:50] Jordan: thanks. Priya, on the helm chart — do you have a sample values for multi‑tenant vs single tenant? our product uses a logical partition per customer.
[00:01:58] Priya: yes. sample values.yaml includes a mode: singleTenant | shared. for NorthStar's model we recommend singleTenant for the adapter to avoid token leakage between partitions. we'll supply the example.
[00:02:12] [00:02:15] Priya: next, network: two supported patterns — VPC peering/direct connect or site‑to‑site VPN. peering is lower latency but requires route propagation and direct peering setup in the marketplace listing. VPN is heavier but easier for initial testing.
[00:02:31] Sana: route propagation — will we need to open outbound to all Redwood IP ranges? we have tight egress rules.
[00:02:36] Marco: you can lock to specific IPs/ports that the helm chart exposes in values. we will give you the final IP ranges once the env is provisioned. for initial staging we can provide a static test IP.
[00:02:48] Liam (Product): is there a recommended MTLS handshake or do you rely on TLS only?
[00:02:52] Priya: mutual TLS is supported for the control plane — we recommend mTLS for added assurance. for data plane we also support tokenized auth and can front it with a customer cert if you prefer.
[00:03:05] [00:03:15] Jordan: switching to marketplace listing — what are the minimal artifacts we need to pass your listing validation?
[00:03:20] Alex: good question. we need: a reference architecture diagram, helm chart tarball, OCI image location, runtime constraints (CPU/GPU profile), test harness results for a baseline load, security checklist (SAML, RBAC notes), and sample customer deployment guide. we'll share a template in the drive.
[00:03:39] Jordan: ok can you also include sample license text and a billing manifest? our procurement team will need it.
[00:03:45] Alex: yes — we'll include a billing manifest skeleton.
[00:03:50] [00:04:05] Priya: Marco, on perf: you ran a small benchmark last week — can you summarize?
[00:04:10] Marco: sure. with our perf harness (scripted using locust and a KV cache warmup), we ran 50 concurrent qps with sequence length ~256 using an open quantized LLM. Dedicated (GPU pool) hit median p95 latency ~120ms per token; Redwood Private (on‑prem) in a VM setup with CPU fallback showed p95 ~480ms in our staging. those are rough numbers; we'll run a NorthStar‑specific test with your model and data shape.
[00:04:37] Sana: that delta is expected given GPU vs CPU. what's required to run the staging perf?
[00:04:43] Marco: we'll need an endpoint that the harness can hit, creds for a service account, and a sample prompt set. we can also run batching experiments — sometimes increasing batch by 2x drops per‑token cost with only slight p99 tail increase.
[00:04:58] [00:05:10] Evan: about logs and retention — what are defaults and can we set retention to 90 days?
[00:05:15] Priya: default is 30 days for request traces in our default plan; for enterprise/private we can extend to 90/365 via config. audit logs we can mirror to your S3 for long‑term retention.
[00:05:27] Jordan: any blockers for cert submission to the marketplace? we want to go live in mid‑Feb.
[00:05:33] Alex: timeline wise — if we get artifacts by Jan 10, we can do a compliance review by Jan 20 and then a final listing test mid‑Feb. so mid‑Feb go‑live is achievable.
[00:05:45] [00:06:00] Sana: integration with SSO — we'll use SAML 2.0 with SCIM for provisioning. do you have a sample metadata file?
[00:06:07] Priya: yes we'll attach a metadata.xml and a SCIM schema. Redwood Console supports SAML + SCIM provisioning and we map groups to RBAC roles. small caveat — SCIM custom attributes need a mapping step in the console for non‑standard claims.
[00:06:20] Liam: can we demo how a new customer lifecycle looks via the marketplace?
[00:06:24] Marco: quick, yes. marketplace flow: customer buys an offer, we provision a tenant stub, then the on‑prem adapter bootstrap runs to register keys and routes. we can show a short flow in the next call.
[00:06:37] [00:06:45] Jordan: about testing — what does the acceptance test look like? we want a checklist for our SREs.
[00:06:50] Priya: acceptance testing we want: connectivity check (TCP/TLS), auth check (token rotate, mTLS), throughput check (50 qps for baseline), failover test (simulate network hiccup), and observability check (traces show end‑to‑end). we'll provide the scripts.
[00:07:12] Sana: any dependencies on Kubernetes version? we run 1.28 in prod.
[00:07:17] Priya: recommended 1.26+; 1.28 is fine but we need to validate CRDs once you supply the cluster access.
[00:07:24] [00:07:30] Evan: security review — do you have a template for penetration testing windows and responsible disclosure?
[00:07:36] Alex: yes, we have a pen test playbook and a responsible disclosure policy. we'll attach both. note that marketplace listing requires a recent pen test or a plan to complete one pre‑release.
[00:07:50] Jordan: okay. on responsibilities for the listing — who owns the listing text and the ref arch diagram?
[00:07:55] Alex: Redwood will provide a reference architecture stub and we ask NorthStar to review and add your branding and specific network details. ownership: Redwood drafts, NorthStar approves.
[00:08:05] [00:08:15] Marco: small note on the adapter lifecycle — upgrades should be done via Helm with canary set to false by default; we support A/B canary if requested. also the adapter writes out a local cache for prefix KV cache and that volume should be set to a durable PVC in values.yaml.
[00:08:31] Jordan: that KV cache — any special recovery semantics? we've seen corruption in quick restarts.
[00:08:35] Priya: we maintain a write‑ahead log; on startup the adapter validates checksum and will rehydrate from S3 snapshot if the local cache is inconsistent. we'll put the exact flags in the manifest.
[00:08:47] [00:08:55] Liam: curious competitor callout — how do you compare to CloudWave? they advertise a simpler marketplace flow.
[00:09:00] Alex: short answer: CloudWave focuses on hosted endpoints and quick integration; Redwood emphasizes production‑grade controls, private deployments, and cost/perf tooling — particularly the Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization.
[00:09:15] Jordan: good. sounds like we have alignment.
[00:09:20] [00:09:30] Priya: next I'll outline a concrete artifact list and timeline. artifact list: helm chart (tar.gz), OCI image URI, values.yaml examples, ref arch diagram, test harness results, SAML metadata, pen test report (or plan), audit log config, billing manifest, README install steps. timeline: deliver artifacts by Jan 10, Redwood compliance review Jan 11-20, staging perf run Jan 21-27, marketplace preflight Feb 1-7, go‑live target Feb 15.
[00:10:00] Sana: Jan 10 is tight but doable. we'll prioritize.
[00:10:04] Jordan: can we get a sample helm test that validates liveness/readiness?
[00:10:08] Priya: yes — we'll include helm test and a kube‑conformance quick script.
[00:10:15] [00:10:30] Alex: ok let's call out owners briefly: Priya — helm & install docs; Marco — perf harness; Jordan/Sana — infra diagram + networking; Evan — security items; Alex — marketplace listing and billing.
[00:10:45] Jordan: noted.
[00:10:50] [00:11:00] Liam: one last item — rollback strategy. if an adapter upgrade causes degradation, what's the fast rollback?
[00:11:06] Marco: Helm rollback to previous release is the primary path. we also keep model snapshots and KV cache backups. for severe incidents we have a kill‑switch that routes traffic to Redwood Hosted fallback for customers who opt in. we'll document the SLA and failover behavior.
[00:11:25] Evan: will that fallback leak logs to Redwood? we need to know data residency implications.
[00:11:30] Priya: good call out. fallback to hosted will only include metadata unless you opt into log forwarding. we can redact PII and we support a no‑export policy for regulated customers.
[00:11:45] [00:11:50] Alex: I think that's a good place to wrap. quick recap and owners — Alex will send marketplace template and SOC/ISO docs; Priya will upload helm checklist and values by Jan 5; Marco will run the first perf with NorthStar test prompts and share results Jan 12; Jordan will send network diagram by Dec 28; Evan will confirm KMS provider by Jan 8.
[00:12:15] Jordan: agreed. thanks everyone.
[00:12:18] Alex: thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the mini‑demo and the perf window.
[00:12:25] (call ends)

Notes: transcription contains occasional word swaps (e.g., "K V cache" spelled out, "SOC two" instead of SOC 2 in one spot). References shared: https://redwood.example.com/marketplace-template (placeholder), shared drive: //redwood/northstar-onboarding (placeholder), perf harness repo: https://github.com/redwood/perf-harness (placeholder).
